query: A 47-year-old man is brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after he was involved in a motor vehicle collision. On arrival, he is unconscious and unresponsive to painful stimuli. His pulse is 120/min, respirations are 10/min, and his blood pressure is 88/60 mm Hg. Infusion of 0.9% saline is begun, and intubation is attempted without success. Pulse oximetry on 20 L/min of oxygen via bag mask shows an oxygen saturation of 78%. The next appropriate step in the management of this patient involves passing a tube through an incision through which of the following structures?
